evidence.notes: All three builds converge on the same sound incident-workspace IA: context, then telemetry tabs, then AI investigation, then remediation cards, with an owners/timeline aside. All preserve the backend contract and selectors, make only GET calls on load, gate by server allowedActions, and split approve and execute into confirmed dialogs with receipts and rollback, so none triggers a critical failure. X is the most accessibility-clean (0 axe issues, skip link, roving tabs) and has the most robust polling and failure handling. Its remediation section is buried at the bottom and its overview list is not triaged. Y adds a section jump-nav, per-remediation steppers, keyboard-readable charts with a table alternative and severity triage, at the cost of one serious axe issue. Z has the strongest AI-evidence governance (citation verification) and the strictest confirmation ladder, but trails on accessibility (no skip link, contrast violations, non-roving tabs) and swallows poll errors silently. The differences are small, with X and Y roughly tied at the top and Z slightly behind on accessibility and state handling.

scorer_rationale.task_hierarchy: The incident header has an in-page section nav (Overview, Telemetry, Investigation, Remediation, Timeline). Each remediation card shows an Approve, Execute, Verify stepper that makes the decision stage obvious. The /incidents list is triaged with active incidents first by severity. The remediation section is still the last main block.
scorer_rationale.domain_adaptation: The layout is organised around the incident and its evidence. Customer impact gets its own callout, and ownership and on-call sit in a sidebar next to the timeline. Citations focus the telemetry view and pick out the exact log line from its excerpt, with a note when no line matches. Telemetry has a service scope selector shared across tabs and a metrics 'Show as table' toggle.
scorer_rationale.contract_preservation: No backend files changed, and routes and test IDs are kept. The page uses the server's filters and sends version and approvalId. A test asserts that no non-GET requests fire on load, and loadRequests are all GETs.
scorer_rationale.interaction_state: Covers skeletons, empty states, retryable errors, the 'Read-only access' notice from the server, 'Someone else changed this record' with a 'Reload latest' action, and partial metrics marked 'Unavailable' instead of zero. It also shows 'Lost contact… retrying' during polling, failed-at-step recovery naming the owner for irreversible changes, and a succeeded state telling the user to confirm recovery in telemetry.
scorer_rationale.responsive: No overflow at any width. Tables become labelled cards on mobile, with short role labels and a compact header. The layout recomposes by moving the ownership and timeline aside below the main content. At 375 the section nav is truncated (detail-375.png).
scorer_rationale.accessibility: Includes a skip link, a 2px solid focus outline (focus shot shows it clearly), and 30 of 30 keyboard stops visible. Metric charts support arrow-key readout, confidence and error budget use role=meter, and forced-colors and reduced-motion media rules are present. Dialogs are portaled, trap focus and restore it. Axe reports 1 serious scrollable-region-focusable issue on the detail page.
scorer_rationale.visual_consistency: Clean and enterprise-appropriate. The health stat tiles are tinted by severity instead of decorative, and the section headers have explanatory subtitles. The remediation cards are fairly dense, with a nested op-grid inside each card.
scorer_rationale.maintainability: Clear split between app/features/pages/ui, a generic useLoad/usePoll and shared primitives. The evidence focusForRef helper is isolated. Remediations.tsx is large at about 745 lines.
scorer_rationale.ai_governance: The investigation form shows scope checkboxes and a billable-run disclosure before a separate 'Start billable investigation' submit, and results show actual vs estimated cost and model. Approve is its own dialog ('Approving does not run anything'). Execute needs an acknowledgement, plus typing the service name for high-risk or irreversible changes, and states which approval ID is used. The receipt includes a copyable audit ref, and rollback lists the steps and changes it will revert.

overfitting.dominant_ia: incident workspace with section jump-nav: impact/overview → telemetry → investigation → remediation stepper cards; ownership + timeline aside; overview = health strip + triaged table
suspicious_patterns: health stat tiles row (mild KPI pattern, but severity-toned and paired with impacted list)

strengths: section nav for long incident page
test asserting no mutations on load
keyboard-readable metric charts and table alternative
precise stale/permission copy tied to server codes
defects: investigation start form is expanded by default and takes up space before any results exist
